historical_record.description: The house was built as a detached single-family home, one of four on this side of the block that Walter Falch designed this year and that began house construction in Balboa Terrace, before Harold Stoner became the tract's main architect.

The house became an artist collective and immersive folk-art environment, with hundreds of artists covering its porch, roofline and ground-floor rooms in mosaics, murals, tapestries, dioramas and sculpture; its nine themed rooms retell the Thousand and One Nights through San Francisco history and are open to the public on guided tours and at events.
The Board of Supervisors adopted a resolution initiating landmark designation of the house as The Gregangelo Museum.
The Historic Preservation Commission held a hearing and recommended the property for landmark designation, including its publicly accessible ground-floor art interiors.
Designated San Francisco Landmark No. 318, The Gregangelo Museum.
